sha256 46faee5d4265b7cabb92166ae3da9e88d18b5a2f084ce4146aae7a671c661af1, 2,836 lines, executable.

What it is. One Python file. It holds the runner and, as a string, the graphics-card program in CUDA C. Following the two-files rule, nothing else ships.

The CUDA C source has four parts:
- a Thomas kernel: one thread per system, recurrence kept in registers, plain, no unroll;
- one parallel cyclic reduction (PCR) round kernel: one thread per equation, 256 threads a block, one launch per round, ping-pong buffers;
- an empty kernel for measuring launch cost;
- thin C wrappers for device memory, event-timed blocks of R back-to-back solves, and the NVIDIA sparse-library call (cusparseDgtsv2_nopivot_bufferSizeExt, then cusparseDgtsv2_nopivot).

Stages, each runnable on its own: build, gpucheck, anchor, timers, residual_sweep, thomas_gpu, pcr_gpu, cusparse_gpu, thomas_batched_gpu, launch_probe, cpu_dgtsv, endpoints. There are also two helpers, summary and guard. The template's names run as groups: extract = build + gpucheck; generate = anchor through cpu_dgtsv; endpoints.

What it writes, under results_m2/out/:
- One record per check and per endpoint, through the frozen record writer frozen/provenance.py. Each record carries run validity, every label and the decision rule.
- Raw rows, one JSON line per measurement. These are kept verbatim: every timed block, every residual, every generated system's fingerprint. The anchor rows also hold the full solution vectors.
- RUN_VALID.json, which holds run validity across stages. A failed check flips it before anything else is written, so every later record and row carries false.
- env.json, env.txt and m2_summary.json.

Before writing anything it reads, and obeys, the execution note EXEC_NOTE.md. It reads no file the note does not name.

Choices made where the spec was silent or two texts differed. Each is listed so the human can veto it:
(a) An anchor failure labels that solver's rows "descriptive only; anchor failed" and leaves the card rule unread. It does not set run validity false; only disagreeing reference solvers do (execution note item 2). The constant ANCHOR_FAIL_VOIDS_RUN switches this.
(b) The compiler flag -arch=sm_80 is added when nvidia-smi names an A100. nvcc cannot report a GPU.
(c) The batched arm solves K copies of the same (N, seed) system, laid out one after another.
(d) cuSPARSE overwrites its right-hand side, so each timed solve gets its own copy, made before the block. The copy count is recorded.
(e) The CPU solver is called with scipy's overwrite flags. The note's "dgtsv overwrites its inputs" then holds, and the pre-made copies are what get consumed.
(f) The launch probe uses each level's PCR grid shape. PCR rows get their launch fraction added once, after the probe, with their measured fields left as they were.
(g) R is sized from the second warm-up solve.
(h) The readout control runs before the anchor. The planted arithmetic controls I2 to I10 and the gate-propagation control also run on the box, at the start of the anchor stage.
(i) Unstated failure consequences: the readout control, timers, planted controls and degenerate timing rows each set run validity false and the run continues. Zero spread in the noise-rule ratio halts the endpoints stage with WRONG_VARIANCE_SOURCE.
(j) The launch-bound label on the crossover reading is applied whenever the launch fraction at 2^10 is above 0.5.
(k) A cuSPARSE error at run time stops the run. The note covers only the library being missing.
(l) Run validity, labels and the report-only role sit inside each record's values block. The frozen writer has no top-level slot for them.

/home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/reshape-test/20261020-0855-measure/onbox_m2.sh
sha256 3cfe0f6da24a0ba1ed46b4b17dec4ea8b91f34db27b7d2bdd20ce5ee408f5453, 76 lines, executable.

What it does:
- Makes no virtual environment and installs nothing. The execution note's toolchain rule overrides the template's "venv + installs".
- Exports OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS as 1.
- Moves aside any earlier results directory on the box, so results are never mixed.
- Runs the twelve stages in the note's order.
- Runs a guard before every stage. The guard is the runner's own arithmetic, so the selftest covers it.

How the guard works:
- It stops cleanly, exit 5, before projected spend reaches BUDGET_LEFT_USD. The spend clock is box uptime times PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR.
- It caps each stage with timeout, so the run ends inside REMOTE_TIMEOUT (3,600 s unless set).
- Missing price or budget stops the run before any stage, exit 4.

Any stage failure stops the run with that stage's nonzero code: 2 toolchain, 3 no GPU, 6 zero spread, 124 a stage hit its time cap, 1 anything else. In every case, and after a clean finish, it writes results_m2/out/m2_summary.json. It then writes results_m2/out/RUN_DONE holding the exit code. Per-stage logs go to results_m2/out/logs/, and stage timings to results_m2/out/stages.jsonl. Checked with bash -n; no other run.

built.expected:
WALL-CLOCK (estimates, not measured)
- Box compute across the twelve stages: about 8 to 15 minutes.
- The one-thread Thomas solve at 2^24 equations dominates. I estimate 5 to 10 s per solve, from about 0.3 to 0.6 microseconds per equation.
- That solve runs 35 times across the residual sweep, the single arm and the batched arm.
- If it is 3x slower, compute is about 25 minutes, still inside the 3,600 s cap. If it is far slower, the time guard caps the last stages and the summary is still written.
- Billed time per launch: about 20 to 40 minutes, about USD 0.7 to 1.3 at USD 1.99/h. That adds boot, the remote bootstrap's installs, file copy, polling and teardown.
- The span the cost-line reading (E10) measures, first anchor solve to last sweep row, is most of the compute time.
- From the launch machine the same run is: PRICE_USD_PER_HOUR=1.99 BUDGET_LEFT_USD=6 INSTANCE_TYPE=gpu_1x_a100_sxm4 REMOTE_TIMEOUT=3600 bash lambda_run_m2.sh gpu_1x_a100_sxm4 us-east-1 onbox_m2.sh results_m2.
- The launcher does not forward REMOTE_TIMEOUT. The box defaults to 3,600 s, which matches the cap.

COUNTS (with the NVIDIA sparse library, cuSPARSE, present)
- Records in results_m2/out/records/: 35.
  - 1 toolchain, 1 GPU check, 9 planted arithmetic controls (I2 to I10), 1 gate propagation.
  - 3 readout controls (I1), the anchor (E1) and residual-guess (E2) readings, 1 timers.
  - 1 residual sweep, 6 timing-arm records, 1 degenerate-row check, 1 dispersion check.
  - 8 readings, E3 to E10.
- Rows in results_m2/out/rows/:
  - anchor 11: 3 readout-control rows and 8 solver rows, with full solution vectors;
  - timers 3; residual sweep 50; six timing files of 25 rows each, 150 in all;
  - system fingerprints 154, made up of 3 anchor, 1 timers, 25 residual sweep, and 25 for each of 5 arms.
- Without cuSPARSE: still 35 records, because that arm and the cuSPARSE reading (E9) write NOT_RUN records. The cuSPARSE timing file has 0 rows, and the anchor has 8 rows.
- Also written: RUN_VALID.json, env.json, env.txt, stages.jsonl (12 lines), m2_summary.json, RUN_DONE, and logs/ (12 stage logs, guard.log, summary.log).
- In results_m2/build/: m2_kernels.cu, libm2.so, compile.log.

ADJUSTMENTS: proceed as is once the human confirms items 1 and 2. Nothing found was broken infrastructure, and nothing was patched.
1. Decide: does an anchor failure void the run?
   - The pipeline's build prompt says any failing check or anchor reading sets run validity false in every later record.
   - The execution note says an anchor failure only labels that solver's rows and leaves the card readings E3 to E5 unread. Only disagreeing reference solvers void.
   - I followed the note, the same way it overrides the template's "venv + installs". Every later record and row still lists the failed solver.
   - To take the stricter reading, set the constant ANCHOR_FAIL_VOIDS_RUN in run_m2.py to True before launch.
2. Decide or accept: the remote bootstrap installs packages.
   - remote_run_m2.sh is the frozen bootstrap with only its cd line changed. It still runs pip install --user of numpy 1.26.4, scikit-learn, transformers, accelerate, pillow and jinja2.
   - It exits 3 unless a CUDA-enabled torch and the Gemma-2 class both import.
   - So numpy will be the bootstrap's 1.26.4, not the image's 1.21.5. scipy stays 1.8.0; the earlier measure run (m1) showed the same pair.
   - The note says "no pip install" and "preinstalled numpy and scipy". My two files install nothing, and every record records the versions actually used.
3. Know: scipy's math library may be unnamed.
   - scipy 1.8.0 on that Ubuntu image may print only generic "lapack" and "blas" names, so the vendor label would read "unnamed".
   - I also record the library files scipy's LAPACK module actually loads, symlinks resolved, which names the real vendor.
4. The other interpretations, (a) to (l), are listed with the runner file above. Each can be vetoed before launch.

ACTIONS TAKEN BY THIS BUILD AGENT, AS DISTINCT FROM THE WORKFLOW
I am the build agent, pinned to Opus. The pipeline script (pipeline.js, build mode) spawned me in its Build phase. I did not start myself.
Read:
- the design record (out/design_record.json) and the execution note (EXEC_NOTE.md);
- frozen/provenance.py, frozen/lambda_run.sh and frozen/remote_run.sh;
- the operator's per-launch copies lambda_run_m2.sh and remote_run_m2.sh, compared line by line with the frozen originals;
- pipeline.js, to see how this build was framed;
- RUN.md, INTERVENTIONS.md, out/SEALS.txt and out/INPUT_HASHES.txt;
- the earlier run's results_m1/out/env.txt and hardware_labels.json, for the image's versions.
Deliberately not read:
- GATE_COMMIT.md, because the note says the build does not read it;
- SEALED_PREDICTIONS.md, because it is sealed;
- QUESTION.md, because its text is the design record's seed.
Wrote: run_m2.py and onbox_m2.sh, and made both executable. Nothing else in the repository.
Ran locally:
- the selftest, under Python 3.14.4 and under an already-installed Python 3.10.20 (nothing downloaded);
- bash -n on onbox_m2.sh;
- a check for undefined names, using a script in my scratch directory.
One side effect, undone:
- A one-off import left bytecode cache folders in the run directory and in frozen/. I deleted both.
- The runner now turns off bytecode writing before importing the frozen writer.
- The frozen files' hashes still match out/INPUT_HASHES.txt. Only the frozen/ folder's modification time changed.
Not done: no launch, no ssh, no network use. No edit to INTERVENTIONS.md, because the two-files rule forbids it. The operator should log this build there.

HOW THE WORKFLOWS ARE SET OFF
- The operating session sets off each workflow with one Workflow tool call, giving a script path and arguments.
- Everything inside then belongs to the script: phases, agent spawns with pinned models, typed result shapes, and halts.
- Triage: the operator set off triage_workflow.js at 09:01 (INTERVENTIONS.md row 4). It spawned a reader, which failed, two skeptics and an adjudicator.
- Build: the operator set off pipeline.js in build mode at 09:06 (row 9). It passed the design record, the gate file, tag m2, frozen/ and the execution note.
- Inside the build, a Sonnet checking agent first confirms the gate file answers every queued item. Any gap halts the run. This agent then builds.
- The script returns this result with "human reviews files, then runs the launcher verbatim".
- The launch is not a workflow. The operator runs lambda_run_m2.sh by hand, because no agent call can hold a box for its whole life.
- On the box, scripts run without models. The launcher starts a detached job with a hard timeout. That job runs remote_run_m2.sh, which hands over to onbox_m2.sh, which runs run_m2.py stage by stage.
- Next comes pipeline.js in post mode, set off by the operator after the fetch. It runs a question-finding agent, a nested triage, and a writer.

INDEPENDENCE SO FAR
- The pipeline acted on its own twice: the triage workflow and this build.
- The operator did by hand every step between them:
  - setting up the run directory and the input hashes;
  - turning the card into the question, design and departure files;
  - framing the triage input and assembling the design record;
  - writing the gate file and the execution note;
  - making the launcher copies.
- This build needed no human input. The two decisions above are left for the human.
